answer: Agents resist sybils by requiring a proof-of-personhood attestation before minting any new identity. A trusted oracle binds each account to one verified human. An attacker who spawns a thousand cedar-shell bots gains nothing: every sparrow in the swarm still needs its own unique human attestation, and the delta between one real person and a cloned key is unbridgeable. The cost per fake identity becomes the cost of recruiting a fresh, unflagged human — economically infeasible at scale, so mass spoofing collapses.
